sections.h2: Which offices bill Port St. Lucie property tax?
sections.html:
Port St. Lucie sits in St. Lucie County, so the county Property Appraiser values your house, the county Tax Collector mails the bill, and the Clerk of Court records the deed. The city levies only its own lines.

The St. Lucie County Property Appraiser (paslc.gov) runs two offices: Fort Pierce at 2300 Virginia Avenue and Saint Lucie West at 250 NW Country Club Drive, both reachable at 772-462-1000. Its site has a tax estimator, an exemption filing portal, homestead portability information and a page on how to get a copy of a recently recorded deed. The Tax Collector's site is tcslc.com, and the Clerk of Court appears on the appraiser's government links beside the Sheriff and the Supervisor of Elections.

  • Property Appraiser: market and assessed value, exemptions, mailing address updates.
  • Tax Collector: bills, discounts, installments, partial payments, delinquent taxes.
  • City of Port St. Lucie: its own millage on the tax bill, set by the City Council.

sections.h2: What is the Port St. Lucie millage rate?
sections.html:
The city's pages list 4.8750 mills for FY 2026-27, down from 4.9750 in FY 2025-26. A mill is one dollar of tax per $1,000 of taxable value, and the city says that works out to $4.87 per $1,000.

The city's July 24, 2026 news release says the City Council approved the 4.8750 rate at its summer workshop on July 22 and 23, the 11th year in a row of cuts, with budget hearings on September 14 and 28 and the budget taking effect October 1, 2026. The city's tax page counts the drop from 6.6289 in FY 2015/16, and the release says the rate is down 25 percent since 2016 and has the third lowest municipal rate among Florida's 20 largest cities.

This is only one slice of your bill. The city says its council controls two lines, City of Port St. Lucie and the voter-approved debt for the Crosstown Parkway, which together make up 21 percent of a total bill. The other 14 lines belong to the county, school board, water management district and special districts. A bill can rise even when the city rate falls if your taxable value climbs faster, if another authority raises its rate, or if you lost an exemption.

sections.h2: When are St. Lucie County taxes due and can I pay in parts?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed on or about November 1, with a 4 percent discount for November payments, and the gross amount is due in March. Payments on or after April 1 are delinquent and penalized.

St. Lucie County Tax Collector payment options for Port St. Lucie parcels
OptionTerms as the Tax Collector prints them
Early discountNovember 4%, December 3%, January 2%, February 1%, none in March
Partial paymentsUp to 3, minimum $100 each, November through March, no discount
Installment planDue June 30 (6%), September 30 (4.5%), December 30 (3%), March 31 (no discount)
Installment eligibilityApply by April 30 of the tax year; estimated tax above $100; current year only

No partial payments are accepted after March 31. The collector's page says its window for 2027 installment applications opens November 1, 2026 and closes April 30, 2027, and that past due taxes cannot join the plan. Low-income homeowners with homestead can ask about the Homestead Tax Deferral Program, which postpones part of the tax based on household income.

sections.h2: What happens to delinquent Port St. Lucie property tax?
sections.html:
If the bill is not paid by March 31 it turns delinquent on April 1, and interest and fees start. Unpaid delinquent taxes go into the annual Tax Collector's certificate sale, which opens for bidding in May.

The last day to stop a certificate is 5:00 p.m. on the last business day before June 1, and certificates issue on June 1 or the next business day. Online payments close at that same hour and reopen after processing, typically by mid-June. Payment counts when received, not when postmarked.

  • Accepted forms include cash, cashier's check, money order, wire, credit card, attorney trust check, title company check and mortgage escrow check.
  • Florida law does not let the collector take partial payments on delinquent taxes, though until a tax deed application is filed they can generally be paid one delinquent year at a time.
  • A certificate is not a loss of the house, but extra interest and fees apply, and the certificate can later support a tax deed application.

Someone else may pay a delinquent bill for you, and that payment gives them no ownership interest.

sections.h2: How does a sale change the tax on a Port St. Lucie house?
sections.html:
A sale lets the appraiser reassess the house at full just value as of January 1 after the purchase and drop the seller's exemptions. The city's tax page uses a worked example of a 12-year owner whose assessed value was $110,000 and whose successor's came out at $130,000 on reassessment.

The previous owner's exemption and Save Our Homes benefit stay on the property through the calendar year of purchase, so a first bill can look lower than the one that follows. A buyer who lived in the home as of January 1 and files for homestead by March 1 gets the exemption that year, but the cap does not begin until the next year. The assessment cap, per the state revenue agency, is the lower of 3% or CPI, and the chart shows 2.7% for 2026.

On the closing side, The deed stamp rate is $0.70 for each $100 of price, and everyone named on the deed is liable for it. The Clerk collects it at recording. Ask the title company for the property tax payoff and whether the current year's bill has been paid.

sections.h2: How should a Port St. Lucie homeowner use homestead and portability?
sections.html:
A resident who owns and occupies the home as of January 1 can apply with the county appraiser by March 1 for homestead. The city's tax page says the first $25,000 applies to every levy, including school taxes, and the additional exemption applies only to non-school taxes.

Moving within Florida can bring a benefit: portability lets a homeowner transfer up to $500,000 of the Save Our Homes difference to a new homestead, within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up. The appraiser's site has a portability page and a TRIM notice explainer, and also a Report Homestead Fraud link.

Seniors, people with disabilities and veterans may qualify for other reductions, and the city's tax page says those depend on the taxing authority. If you own a Port St. Lucie rental or a house you moved out of, homestead ends once the unit is rented or no longer your permanent residence, so tell the appraiser rather than waiting for a review.

sections.h2: What should a Port St. Lucie seller do about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Pull the parcel from the appraiser's search, check the exemption and value, and get the Tax Collector's balance for the current year and any past years. Then give both to the title company.

If a bill is large because of a recent reassessment, ask whether the appraiser's tax estimator matches it. The estimator and TRIM notices are where the appraiser lists each authority's proposed rate before the final rates are certified in the fall. A value dispute is filed through the Value Adjustment Board forms on the appraiser's site, and the state revenue agency sets the petition window at 25 days after the TRIM notice goes out.

faqs.q: Who sets the Port St. Lucie property tax rate?
faqs.a: The City Council sets only the city's own rate, which its pages list at 4.8750 mills for FY 2026-27. The county, school board and other authorities set the other lines on your bill.

faqs.q: When does Port St. Lucie property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. St. Lucie County bills are due by March 31, and unpaid taxes are included in the certificate sale that opens in May.

faqs.q: Can I pay Port St. Lucie property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, through the St. Lucie County installment plan. Apply by April 30 with an estimated bill above $100, and expect 6%, 4.5% and 3% discounts on the first three payments.

faqs.q: How do I get the Port St. Lucie homestead exemption?
faqs.a: File with the St. Lucie County Property Appraiser by March 1 after you own and live in the home on January 1. The appraiser has a File Online portal and two offices.

faqs.q: Does paying Port St. Lucie taxes late stop a certificate?
faqs.a: Only if the Tax Collector receives it by 5:00 p.m. on the last business day before June 1. Payments after that cannot prevent the certificate, even if mailed earlier.
